abstract: While ambient assisted living (AAL) sensing systems offer promise for aging in place, their impacts on professional caregivers are overlooked. We conducted two collective speculation workshops (N=24) with personal health aides (PHAs, n=18) and certified nursing assistants (CNAs, n=6) to examine the ethical implications and value tensions of a care system with ambient intelligence (CSAI), our conceptualization of an AAL. Participants anticipated different implications across care roles and settings. PHAs anticipated additional responsibilities from CSAI, including learning how it operates and supporting older adults in its use. CNAs, who had greater access to workplace resources and protections, similarly noted that CSAI could create additional work. Participants also identified tensions around visibility, as sensing could support caregivers by documenting difficult working conditions while simultaneously making their behavior more vulnerable to misinterpretation. Through their modifications and surfaced discussions, we propose design guidelines for AAL systems, such as integrating context-aware sensing.

ob.ai_reason: 聚焦环境智能照护系统及照护者伦理
ob.tldr: 面向居家养老的环境智能照护系统常忽视专业照护者。通过24名护理员参与的集体推测工作坊，识别出技术学习、额外工作及行为误读等价值张力，并提出情境感知等系统设计建议。

title: "We Are the Dirty Hands": Reimagining an Ambient Intelligence Care System with Professional Caregivers
title_zh: “我们就是脏手”：携手专业照护者重塑环境智能照护系统
